name: claudeignore-guard
description: Makes `.claudeignore` work, and enforces `.gitignore` alongside it by default. Claude Code has no native .claudeignore (anthropics/claude-code#579, #4160, #29455) yet blog posts teach it as if it did, so people list .env there and believe they are protected while nothing reads the file. This PreToolUse hook enforces both: Read/Edit/Write/NotebookEdit on an excluded path is denied, and the denial names the exact file and line of the rule plus the '!' line that would allow it. .gitignore is merged in by default so a repo that already keeps secrets out of git is protected with no per-project setup; .claudeignore rules are applied LAST and always win on conflict. CLAUDEIGNORE_NO_GITIGNORE=1 opts out, and because that mode fails silently a SessionStart notice reports how many rules are being skipped. Matching is git's own: each directory's ignore files are concatenated into a scratch mirror and queried with `git check-ignore`, so gitignore semantics (negation, anchoring, **, dir-only rules, nested files, precedence) are exact rather than re-implemented, paths that do not exist yet are answered, and the project need not be a git repository. Freshness uses cp -p .track copies and a bidirectional mtime gate — no cache TTL to tune; discovery of ignore files in new directories is scoped to the session. Does NOT cover Bash or Grep/Glob (see docs); permissions.deny remains the real security boundary. Requires git. Env: CLAUDEIGNORE_DISABLED=1, CLAUDEIGNORE_NO_GITIGNORE=1, CLAUDEIGNORE_MODE=warn, CLAUDEIGNORE_QUIET=1.
